title: Resolution-normalized module/abelian cohomology comparison
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $q\in\mathbf N$. Write $H^q_{\mathrm{mod}}(X,F)$ for module-derived cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], and $H^q_{\mathrm{ab}}(X,F_{\mathrm{ab}})$ for the cohomology of its underlying abelian sheaf [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], represented as Ext from the constant integer sheaf. Define the additive equivalence $E^q_{X,F}:H^q_{\mathrm{mod}}(X,F)\simeq H^q_{\mathrm{ab}}(X,F_{\mathrm{ab}})$ as follows: compute module-derived sections on the standard module injective resolution; forget scalars using exact forgetting of homology; identify the two section complexes; apply the inverse acyclic-resolution comparison for the forgotten resolution; apply the inverse Ext/derived-sections comparison constructed from Hom complexes and the section adjunction; and precompose Ext by the inverse canonical isomorphism from the free abelian sheaf on the terminal representable to the constant integer sheaf. Package this same composite as a natural isomorphism in $F$, and obtain $E^q_{X,F}$ by taking its component and forgetting to an additive equivalence. The site-Ext and site-H identifications are identity isomorphisms. These are specified composites with their specified inverses, with no choice of an arbitrary equivalence.
